Brief Profile of Directors
Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha, aged 57 years, assumed charge as the Chairman & Managing Director (CMD)
of the Company on 16 th October 2023. With more than three decades of distinguished experience in
infrastructure development and financing, he is a seasoned leader with deep expertise in urban infrastructure,
project finance, institutional development and public policy implementation.
Starting his career with a Multinational Company, Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha’s professional journey spans
across various prestigious roles in State PSUs, Private sector Companies and Central Public Sector
Undertakings. Prior to joining HUDCO, he served for over 17 years at REC Limited, a Maharatna NBFC
under the Government of India, where he held several strategic leadership positions, overseeing business
operations, consultancy services and corporate social responsibility initiatives.
At HUDCO, Shri Kulshrestha is driving Company’s transformation into a comprehensive urban infrastructure
financing and advisory institution, aligned with “Viksit Bharat @ 2047” vision of the Government of India.
His leadership focuses on strengthening HUDCO’s role in financing sustainable urbanisation by supporting
projects across housing, urban mobility, water supply, sewerage, Sanitation, social infrastructure and other
critical urban development sectors. Recognised for his strategic perspective on infrastructure financing,
Shri Kulshrestha is committed to positioning HUDCO as India’s premier 360-degree urban infrastructure
solutions provider, delivering integrated financing, advisory and capacity-building services that support
resilient cities, climate-responsive infrastructure and inclusive urban growth.
Leveraging his extensive experience in infrastructure financing, Shri Kulshrestha has consistently advocated
an integrated approach to urban development by fostering close collaboration with State Governments,
Urban Local Bodies, Development Authorities and public agencies. His emphasis on early-stage project
conceptualisation, technical and financial appraisal, institutional capacity building and structured advisory
support is poised to contribute to the development of bankable urban infrastructure projects, enabling States
and implementing agencies to access long-term financing for sustainable development.
Shri Kulshrestha is also spearheading initiatives aimed at broadening HUDCO’s resource base through
diversified market borrowings, optimisation of the Corporation’s cost of funds and enhanced engagement
with domestic and international capital markets. His focus on prudent financial management, digital
transformation, governance excellence and innovation continues to strengthen HUDCO’s institutional
resilience and operational efficiency.
Shri Sanjay Kulshrestha is not holding directorship in any company other than HUDCO.

Distinguished Shareholders,
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you all to your Company's 56 th Annual General Meeting. The enduring support
and trust reposed by our shareholders and stakeholders in our strategic vision and operational excellence have catalysed
the Company's transformation into a diversified Infrastructure Finance Company, aligned with the grand national vision of a
‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 - one that improves lives, creates equitable opportunities and builds sustainable infrastructure for all.
Your Company’s core commitment is ‘Financing Infrastructure for a Viksit Bharat’. Today, HUDCO is playing a vital role in
national development, which is demonstrated by its status as one of India's prestigious Navratna CPSEs. As we look to scale
this impact, we must acknowledge the broader global and domestic macro environment in which we operate.
01 India's Resilience in a Transforming World
As we have all experienced, the year under review unfolded in an increasingly uncertain global environment marked by
geopolitical tensions, evolving trade dynamics, the reconfiguration of global supply chains, rapid advances in Artificial
Intelligence, the growing imperative for climate resilience and sustainability, and the rise of urbanisation as a key driver of
economic growth and societal transformation. Together, these forces are reshaping the way nations compete, invest and
develop.
Against this backdrop, India continued to demonstrate remarkable economic resilience, remaining among the fastest-
growing major economies in the world. While geopolitical developments and volatility in global commodity and energy prices
exerted pressure on inflation and external balances, the Indian economy remained well supported by prudent fiscal and
monetary policie s, resilient domestic demand, sustained public capital expenditure and a strong financial system. These sound
macroeconomic fundamentals continued to reinforce investor confidence and support India's long-term growth trajectory.
While this performance is encouraging, our greatest challenge is not simply to achieve high growth, but to sustain it over the
coming decades. As India's economy expands, the drivers of future growth will need to become broader, stronger and more
productive. In this evolving growth paradigm, urbanisation assumes critical importance.
02 Cities at the Heart of India’s Growth Story
As India advances towards becoming a USD 30 Trillion (~₹2890 Lakh Crore) economy over the next two decades as
envisaged by NITI Aayog, a fundamental question arises: where will this growth originate? The answer lies in India's
cities. Well-planned cities, supported by quality urban infrastructure, will serve as the principal engines of economic
growth, generating significant multiplier effects by crowding in private investment, enhancing productivity, creating
employment, fostering innovation and expanding economic opportunities.
While these benefits are evident across the urban centres, the greatest opportunity now lies beyond the largest metropolitan
cities like Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi. The next chapter of India's growth story will increasingly be driven by Tier-II and

03 Urban Development: Improving Everyday Lives
Economic growth, however, is only one measure of successful urbanisation. The true purpose of urban development is
to improve the everyday lives of people by creating cities that are more liveable, resilient and inclusive. India's future will
therefore be shaped not only by the way it plans, develops and prepares its cities for tomorrow, but also by how effectively
those cities enha nce the quality of life of every citizen. Strong cities are those, where a young family can own an affordable
home, where a commuter spend s less time in traffic because of efficient public transport, where every household has access
to safe drinking water, sanitation and reliable public services, where children grow up in clean and safe neighbourhoods,
where senior citizens can access quality healthcare and public spaces with dignity and where businesses thrive because of
dependable infrastructure and efficient logistics.
The success of urban development is measured not by number of projects completed, but by the
improvement it brings to the everyday lives of people.
These aspirations are becoming increasingly important as India undergoes one of the largest urban transformations in human
history. According to the United Nations projections, India is home to over 55.5 Crore urban residents today and by
2050, the country is projected to reach a significant demographic milestone, with over 50% of our population -
approximately 87.7 Crore people residing in urban areas. Cities contribute nearly 60 percent of India's GDP and their role
as centres of productivity, innova tion, employment and investment will only become more significant in the years ahead. At
the same time, the infrastructure needed to support this transformation is immense. The World Bank estimates that India will
require nearly ~₹80 Lakh Crore in urban infrastructure investment between 2021 and 2036. However, the success of this
investment will not be determined by the amount spent alone, but by how effectively it transforms India's cities into productive,
liveable and resilient urban centres. Meeting this unprecedented urban challenge will require a fundamental rethinking of
how India's cities are planned, financed and developed.

04 Rethinking How We Plan, Finance and Develop Cities Around People
As India builds the cities of a developed nation, it must draw upon global best practices, while adapting them thoughtfully
to its own unique context, reflecting the country's diversity, scale and development priorities. Advanced economies such as
Singapore, Japan and South Korea offer valuable lessons in integrated land use and transport planning, smart infrastructure,
digital governance and climate-resilient urban development. European cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam
demonstrate how walkable neighbourhoods, Complete Streets, protected cycling infrastructure and interconnected
green networks can enhance both liveability and economic productivity.
Planning approaches such as Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), mixed-use development and walk-to-work or
15-minute neighbourhoods further illustrate how bringing homes, workplaces, education, healthcare and essential services
closer together can improve accessibility rather than merely mobility, reduce travel demand and enhance the quality of urban
life. At the same time, countries such as China, Vietnam and Indonesia demonstrate how rapid urbanisation can be supported
through coordinated housing and infrastructure development.
The common lesson across these experiences is that cities achieve their greatest economic potential when infrastructure
is planned as an integrated system rather than as isolated assets . India has made significant strides in expanding
urban infrastructure over the past decade; however, the full multiplier benefits of urbanisation will be realised only when
transport, housing, land use, public services, environmental infrastructure and governance evolve in a coordinated manner.
Such integration not only improves productivity, reduces the cost of doing business and strengthens climate resilience,
but also enhances the ease of living, enabling India's cities to become vibrant, competitive and sustainable engines of
economic growth.

10 Enabling India's Next Phase of Urban Transformation - Developing the Cities of Tomorrow
India is entering a defining phase of its development journey. The coming decades will not merely witness the expansion of our
cities, they will determine how future generations live, work, travel and prosper. The cities of tomorrow must be designed not
merely to accommodate a growing population, but to improve the quality of life of every citizen. They should be people-centric,
accessible and inclusive, where homes, workplaces, education, healthcare and public transport are well integrated .
They should be walkable, transit-oriented and climate-resilient, supported by green corridors, efficient public services and
circular resource systems that maximise the reuse of water, energy and waste. Above all, they should be economically vibrant,
digitally enabled and institutionally strong, creating an urban ecosystem that enhances productivity, sustainability and the
ease of living. HUDCO aspires to contribute to this transformation by combining technical expertise with long-term
development finance, helping States and Urban Local Bodies conceive and implement integrated urban projects that
deliver enduring social, economic and environmental outcomes. Through this approach, the Company seeks not
merely to finance infrastructure, but to help shape cities that improve the everyday lives of people.
Meeting these aspirations will require a new paradigm of urban development - one that prioritises institutional capacity,
financial sustainability and investment readiness alongside infrastructure creation.
The nation can become a ‘Viksit Bharat’ only when our cities become ‘Viksit’. For ‘Viksit Cities’, we need
‘Viksit Urban Local Bodies’ who are the implementors of projects.
Accordingly, the urban development model has to now shift from a grant-based approach to a challenge-based, reform-
oriented and investment-led model , where cities are encouraged to strengthen governance, improve project preparation
and attract long- term capital. This marks a fundamental shift in the way urban infrastructure will be planned, financed and
delivered.
Strengthening the Urban Local Bodies does not mean that they are unable to deliver. In fact, many municipalities have already
shown what is possible through governance reforms, better financial management and successful municipal and green bond
issuances that have received encouraging investor response. The real opportunity now is scaling these successes across
hundreds of smaller cities, which is where institutions like HUDCO can make the greatest difference by supporting project
preparation, capacity building and access to long-term finance.
To realise this vision and build a strong pipeline of future business, HUDCO is deepening its engagement with State
Governments, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and other public sector institutions through long-term strategic partnerships.
These collaborations not only strengthen the Company's future business pipeline but also enable the planning, financing and
implementation of transformative urban infrastructure across the country.

India's rapid urbanisation is creating an unprecedented demand for integrated urban infrastructure, urban redevelopment

one of the Company's most significant long-term growth opportun ities. Building on its extensive experience in housing
finance and integrated urban development, HUDCO will continue to provide long-term financial assistance, consultancy,

solutions for rental housing, integrated townships and housing-linked urban infrastructure.

quality of urban services. Recognising this, HUDCO is expanding its role beyond infrastructure financing to become a
comprehensive partner in strengthening municipal finance and enhancing the creditworthiness of cities.

by supporting project preparatio n, financial structuring, credit enhancement, transaction advisory, municipal bond
issuances and institutional capacity building. These initiatives are aimed at enabling ULBs to become investment-ready
and access diverse sources of long-term capital.

AMRUT 2.0 to support water supply, sewerage and essential urban services. In addition, the announcement of a

Water security is emerging as one of the most critical infrastructure priorities for India's rapidly urbanising economy.

Recognising this evolving landsc ape, HUDCO will continue expanding its financing portfolio across urban water supply,

India's economic landscape is being reshaped by the emergence of City Economic Regions (CERs), Global Capability
Centres (GCCs), Industrial Corridors and Integrated Townships, creating a new generation of demand for urban
infrastructure. These integrated economic ecosystems require significant investments in housing, mobility, water
supply, sewerage, social infrastructure and municipal services, presenting substantial long-term financing opportunities
for HUDCO.

hosts 2,117 Global Capability Centres , employing 23.6 Lakh professionals and generating ~₹9.48 Lakh Crore in

is expected to accelerate investments in integrated urban infrastructure across the country, providing a significant
opportunity for HUDCO to support integrated infrastructure development through customised financing solutions and
strategic partnerships, thereby contributing to India's next phase of economic transformation.

Efficient, sustainable and integrated transport systems are fundamental to India's future economic competitiveness
and urban development. HUDCO has steadily expanded its infrastructure financing portfolio beyond traditional urban
infrastructure to support modern mobility systems that enhance regional connectivity, improve logistics efficiency and
promote sustainable urbanisation.
The scale of investment opportunities remains substantial. The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) envisages
infrastructure investments of over ₹143 Lakh Crore, with the transport sector accounting for the largest share of
investments. Simultaneously, the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is driving integrated, multimodal connectivity
across the country through coordinated infrastructure planning.
Against this backdrop, HUDCO will continue financing Metro Rail, Regional Rapid Transit Systems (RRTS),
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), logistics parks, freight corridors, industrial corridors, ports, airports and
multimodal transport infrastructure. By supporting integrated transport ecosystems, the Company aims to improve
urban mobility, enhance economic productivity and strengthen India's logistics competitiveness.

As Indian cities face increasing risks from heat waves, urban heat islands, urban flooding, cyclones, water
scarcity and other climate-related events , investments in resilient urban infrastructure are expected to increase
significantly over the coming decades.
